synthetic-sent-account-2.html.notes: The second signed-in account (/mail/u/1/), Sent, head of the list. Coverage belongs to this account (its hash), not to the account of synthetic-sent-page-1.html. synthetic-sent-dst-auckland.html.notes: DST edge. Browser time zone Pacific/Auckland: clocks went from 02:00 NZST (+12:00) to 03:00 NZDT (+13:00) on Sun 27 Sep 2026. "Sun, Sep 27, 2026, 3:10 AM" is +13:00 and "1:45 AM" the same day is +12:00, 25 minutes earlier in real time. A parser that applies one fixed offset to every row gets one of them an hour wrong.

synthetic-sent-midnight.html.notes: Read at 00:30 on Sat 3 Oct (America/New_York). Rows 3 and 4 have no time title (a synthetic stress case, not how Gmail renders a list) so their time comes from the relative text: "11:58 PM" read at 00:30 is last night, and "Yesterday, 11:47 PM" is Fri 2 Oct 23:47; both resolve to the minute. Row 2 shows "Oct 2" but its title gives 23:59, and row 5 is exactly midnight at the start of Fri 2 Oct.

expected.subjectHint: Following up on the partnership proposal we discussed at the conference last wee

synthetic-sent-page-1.html.notes: Sent list, first page (Newer is disabled: the head of the list), 10 rows, 11 observations (row 2 has two recipients). Older is enabled, so the list may go on: the window starts one minute after the oldest row's minute (17:55), whose rows are still observations, because a send in that minute older than the oldest row would be on page 2, unseen (QA-1). Edge rows: a U+202F before AM/PM in two time titles; a subject with a double space (collapsed in subjectHint); a recipient address in mixed case (kept exactly as read); "(no subject)" (no subjectHint); a subject over 80 code points (subjectHint is the first 80); an emoji subject (one code point, never split). Seeds sit in snippets and in the screen-reader row summary, never in the subject span. Rows 9 and 10 reappear on page 2.

synthetic-sent-page-2.html.notes: Sent list, second page (rows 11-20 of 26). Two messages were sent between the two reads, so the first two rows here are rows 9 and 10 of page 1, with the same row ids and fields: they must project to the same contentHash (the dedup fact). Not the head of the list, so the pass posts its rows and health OK but no coverage, by design (sprint_2 2.7): in conversation view a send from this span can be listed on page 1 under a later reply's date, so this page's span is not every send in it.

synthetic-sent-thread.html.notes: The Sent row 1 of page 1, opened. The Sent folder is selected but no thread list is on the page, so the Sent observer reads nothing and reports DEGRADED (not_sent_list) with no coverage: an opened thread is not the list. The receipt observer sees an opened message from the account itself, which no parser claims: zero observations. The body holds three seeds.

synthetic-sent-time-unresolved.html.notes: Row 2 has no time title and its text "Oct 1" names a whole day, not a minute, so it cannot become an observation. The pass emits rows 1 and 3, reports DEGRADED and writes no coverage: a row Attest could not read is not evidence that nothing was sent that day (Hard Rule 5). The reasons are the Sprint 2.0 pass contract's (src/observers/plan.ts): the observer hands the untimed row to redact.project without an occurredAt, which refuses it (redact.missing_occurred_at), and its visible window is unknown because an unread row could be the oldest or newest (window.unknown).
